text: Among ERC Consolidator Grant projects classified under textiles, how does the project that set out to make wearable fibres for sensing hazardous gases and mechanical strain produce those fibres?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/textiles%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-COG' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: INTERACT (grant 648763) produces them by electrospinning liquid crystals (LCs) inside a polymer sheath, so that the LC sits in the fibre core and passes its responsiveness to the non-woven textile; thicker LC-core fibres are made with a newly developed microfluidic wet spinning approach.
notes: Filter: fundingScheme = 'ERC-COG' AND a euroSciVoc path under the textiles subtree ('engineering and technology/materials engineering/textiles'). Re-executed this pass: 7 survivors out of 295 projects in the textiles subtree. Exhaustive adjudication (S=7 <= 20, every survivor's objective + report teaser/summary read this pass). 648763 INTERACT: IN - report summary: 'INTERACT explored a new class of responsive textile fibers realized by electrospinning liquid crystals (LCs) inside a polymer sheath, targeting wearable detectors of hazardous gases and sensors of tensile or compressive strain', and 'Thicker LC core fibers can be realized by means of a newly developed microfluidic wet spinning approach'; objective adds 'the concept of liquid crystal (LC) electrospinning ... incorporating the LC in the fiber core'. 682711 PENELOPE: OUT - weaving as a technical mode of existence; no fibre production, no sensing. 726195 RE-FASHIONING: OUT - Renaissance dress; it does dye- and fibre ANALYSIS of historical textiles, but makes no wearable sensing fibres. 771288 TextileLab: OUT - economic history of cotton manufacturing relocation. 819458 PoliticsOfPatents: OUT - sociology of clothing patents and citizenship. 101002711 BODYinTRANSIT: OUT - the closest in-filter near-miss; it builds wearable multisensory feedback devices, but spins no fibres and senses neither gases nor strain. 101003104 MYCLOTH: OUT - geometric modelling of personalized garments. Filter-discrimination (unscoped pooled search on the recorded question text, k=10, four conditions): the gold is NOT an unambiguous top-1 - 648763 ranks lexical 2, dense 10, hybrid 7, hybrid_rerank 1, while the unscoped top-1s are 704963 E-TEX (lexical, hybrid) and 739891 Wearonics (dense). The filter removes these competing text-satisfiers, all of which make wearable sensing fibres: 704963 E-TEX (MSCA-IF-EF-ST, textiles-tagged, 'conductive textile fibres ... built directly on textile fibres', 'truly wearable sensing applications'), 739891 Wearonics (MSCA-IF-EF-ST, textiles+sensors+fibers-tagged, 'develop stretchable conductive fibres (SCF) using silver nanowires and spandex fibre', used 'for measuring respiration and body motions'), 842349 SENFLEX (ERC-POC, 'truly smart and flexible fibers called SenFlex, that can be elastically deformed and sense the imposed mechanical constraints'), 637624 ThermoTex (ERC-STG, textiles+sensors-tagged, thermoelectric fibres and yarns for wearable electronic textiles - ERC but not COG, so the scheme VALUE is what cuts), 796640 GFSMART (MSCA-IF-EF-CAR, textiles-tagged, graphene fibre based antennas for smart textiles), 834966 STREAM (MSCA-IF, textiles-tagged, optical fibre sensors produced by a microfluidic device and integrated into textiles), 685758 1D-Neon (IA, 'Piezo-based F-Stretch and Fibre-Sensor achieved'), 825232 WEAFING (RIA, coated yarn actuators woven into fabrics). Text is load-bearing: no stored column says how the fibres are made - the title ('Intelligent Non-woven Textiles and Elastomeric Responsive materials by Advancing liquid Crystal Technology') names neither electrospinning nor the polymer sheath; the method lives only in the objective and report summary. term_style re-derived for this wording: the question keeps 'wearable' and 'hazardous gases' verbatim from the gold report summary (it paraphrases only 'tensile or compressive strain' as 'mechanical strain' and deliberately omits the mechanism vocabulary, which is the answer), and the rank matrix agrees with exact-term - gold is lexical rank 1 scoped and lexical rank 2 unscoped. Scoped pooled search over the 7 survivors on the recorded text: 648763 lexical 1, dense 1, hybrid 1, hybrid_rerank 2 (726195 RE-FASHIONING takes rerank 1 on its dye/fibre-analysis chunk but is adjudicated OUT on the text).

text: Among the SME Instrument phase 1 projects classified under viticulture, how do the ones that build on a producer's own naturally occurring organisms, rather than on bought-in standard cultures, put those organisms to work in making wine?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle = 'viticulture' AND p.fundingScheme = 'SME-1' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Two of the 14 SME Instrument phase 1 projects tagged viticulture take this route, and both make the producer's own resident biology the source of a wine competitors cannot replicate. MYBIOASSET (LEV2050) treats a winery's own bio-imprint as a commercial asset: it genetically selects, preserves and reproduces indigenous yeasts of different strains, so a house can keep dependable, robust fermentation and still bottle singular wines, the firm's stated aim being to recover the old diversity of wines without giving up modern production technology. Eternum works from the vineyard outwards: Bodegas Langa, with 150 years of winemaking expertise, profiles the vineyard's own microbiology and uses that profile both to draw up a highly specific low-impact pest control plan and to pick the site's own fermentation yeasts, then matures the wine together with those yeasts in a purpose-designed container that mimics the shape of a maturation deposit, so nutrients the organisms yield keep enriching the wine inside the bottle. The shared move is to replace a bought-in standardised input with an on-site biological one, LEV2050 packaging it as a technology any winery can buy and Bodegas Langa applying it to its own estate's production.
notes: Filter: fundingScheme='SME-1' (SME Instrument phase 1) AND euroSciVoc leaf 'viticulture'. Observed values: viticulture is a LEAF with no sub-terms - a DISTINCT euroSciVocPath/euroSciVocTitle query on LIKE '%viticulture%' returns exactly one path, 'agricultural sciences/agriculture, forestry, and fisheries/agriculture/horticulture/viticulture' (46 projects), so the subtree reading (path LIKE '%/viticulture%') and the leaf reading (euroSciVocTitle='viticulture') are the same 46 projects and 'classified under viticulture' has exactly one executable reading. Scheme spread over those 46: SME-1 14, SME-2 6, IA 6, RIA 5, MSCA-IF 3, CSA 3, MSCA-IF-EF-ST 3, MSCA-RISE 3, ERC-POC 1, MSCA-ITN-ETN 1, MSCA-IF-EF-RI 1 - the scheme half cuts 46 to 14. Corpus-wide the only SME schemes are SME-1 (4228), SME-2 (1389), SME (86), SME-2b (31); 'phase 1' = SME-1, and no viticulture project carries plain 'SME' or 'SME-2b'. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE (S=14 <= 20): all 14 survivors read via get_project_text (objective + report teaser), 2 IN and 12 OUT. IN: 711328 MYBIOASSET (LEV2050) - selects, preserves and reproduces indigenous yeasts so a winery can bottle unrepeatable wine while keeping robust fermentation; 826866 Eternum (Bodegas Langa) - analyses the vineyard's microbiome, selects indigenous fermentation yeasts, matures the wine with those yeasts in a novel container. OUT: 674409 UVT (UV light KILLS microorganisms in beverage tanks - the opposite of building on them); 674786 VitiPrecision 2020 (computer vision and sensors for vineyard information, no organisms); 773813 TX3 (electric transaxle for farm vehicles); 775049 TEVINS (vision-guided vineyard sprayer); 781608 LBS-PROTECTION (liquid bioassimilable sulphur against powdery mildew - a chemical formulation, not the producer's own organisms); 815904 ANTOFERINE (polyphenols extracted from vineyard waste - plant matter, applied post-harvest to fruit and vegetables, not to making wine); 816093 SSR (mechanical shoot remover); 832214 Winegrid (fibre-optic vinification sensors); 855467 Eco-Closure (recyclable bottle closure); 863346 BIOAVENGER (bio-fungicide made from MycoSolutions' own fungi, sold in and applied to soil for crop protection - not the producer's own organisms and not winemaking); 876252 PPB (bottle cleaning and polishing line); 877334 DSES (wireless power-tool safety system). Non-embedding sweeps over the survivors: regexp over objectives for yeast|microb|ferment|indigenous|native|microorganism|strain|bacteri|fungi|fungal hit only 674409, 711328, 815904, 826866, 863346; regexp over report teaser+summary+workPerformed+finalResults for yeast|indigenous|autochthon|native|microbio|microbiome|microbiota|ferment hit only 711328 and 855467 (Eco-Closure's hit is 'second fermentation ... methode Champenoise' plus cork-taint fungus - OUT). Both sweeps confirm the exhaustive read; no additional gold. Filter-discrimination (unscoped pooled, k=10, same question text): text-satisfying projects OUTSIDE the filter - 881239 ECOBIOMASS (fundingScheme SME-2, viticulture-tagged, same firm LEV2050: 'produce personalized wines using selected indigenous microorganisms', dense rank 2, hybrid_rerank rank 1), 643063 MICROWINE (MSCA-ITN-ETN, viticulture-tagged, microbial community from vineyard soil through fermentation, dense 3, hybrid_rerank 3), 747775 Mitogression (MSCA-IF-EF-RI, not viticulture-tagged, engineered wine yeast strains, dense 6). Unscoped, the gold pair ranks BELOW ECOBIOMASS (MYBIOASSET rerank 5, Eternum rerank 6), so the text alone does not identify the gold set. Text side is not answerable from any stored column: how each project puts the organisms to work exists only in objective and report prose. term_style=paraphrase: the question avoids the gold texts' distinctive vocabulary (yeast, indigenous, microorganism, microbiome, microbiota, fermentation, vinification, bio-imprint) and uses 'naturally occurring organisms' and 'bought-in standard cultures'; in the scoped rank matrix lexical puts non-gold VitiPrecision 1st and gold MYBIOASSET only 7th, while dense puts Eternum 1st and MYBIOASSET 2nd - gold is reached semantically, not by term overlap. pooling_evidence reports the SCOPED pooled search and nothing else, on one denominator: pooled_candidate_count=11 distinct survivors returned across the four conditions (711328, 826866, 674786, 815904, 832214, 855467, 674409, 876252, 775049, 863346, 781608; not returned: 773813, 816093, 877334), accepted=2, rejected_count=9. The gold label itself does NOT come from that pool: it comes from the separate exhaustive adjudication of all 14 survivors recorded above (2 IN, 12 OUT), which is the authority for gold, while the scoped pool only diagnoses retrievability and term_style.

text: Among the graphene projects that include a Swedish participating organisation, how is graphene itself being used to fight antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%graphene%' AND o.country = 'SE' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Two of the 18 graphene-classified projects with a Swedish participant use graphene against drug-resistant bacteria: PANG (Pathogen and Graphene, MSCA-RISE) and PEST-BIN (MSCA-ITN). PANG chemically functionalises graphene structures with antibacterial peptides and molecules such as menthol to build graphene-based antibacterial matrixes, tests their bactericidal potential against AMR strains, and exploits the photothermal properties of rGO so that suspensions and transdermal patches can kill pathogens by non-invasive photothermal therapy, while also studying the mechanism of action and the effect on the immune system. PEST-BIN applies graphene in two complementary ways: functionalised graphene-based sensors on disposable chips made essentially of carbon and biodegradable polymers, whose receptors capture biomarkers from the bacterial surface for fast infection diagnostics, and antibacterial graphene coatings on magnetic nanoparticles and hydrogel/polymer surfaces that carry antibacterial molecules into bacterial biofilms. Both treat graphene as an alternative route around antimicrobial resistance rather than as another antibiotic, and both are training networks that build the capability alongside the technology.
notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'engineering and technology/nanotechnology/nano-materials/two-dimensional nanostructures/graphene' (the only path matching LIKE '%graphene%'; 290 projects corpus-wide) AND at least one organization row with country='SE' (any role). Re-executed this pass: 18 survivors, matching the corpus-profile seed (no drift). ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, all 18 survivors read via get_project_text objective+teaser): IN 690836 PANG - objective and report summary are entirely about graphene-based nanocomposites/matrixes against multi-drug-resistant bacteria; IN 955626 PEST-BIN - graphene-functionalised diagnostic chips and antibacterial graphene coatings against antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections. OUT (no antibacterial/antimicrobial use of graphene in any text): 641416 iPUBLIC (inkjet-printed graphene energy storage), 646155 INSPIRED (industrial-scale nanomaterial inks for printed electronics), 650029 TAIPI (CSA on FET Flagship impact assessment), 686135 PROCETS (anti-wear/anti-corrosion protective coatings), 696656 GrapheneCore1 / 785219 GrapheneCore2 / 881603 GrapheneCore3 (Flagship core projects; composites, photonics, batteries, water purification - no bacteria/antibiotic mention anywhere in objective or report text), 721991 GreenCarbon (biomass-derived carbons), 758935 1D-Engine (quasi-1D superconductivity theory), 764977 mCBEEs (corrosion of micro/nanodevices; its only infection mention is Cu/Zn/Ag nanoparticle decoration of implantable alloys to 'reduce infection risks', not graphene), 810451 HERO (hidden orders in quantum matter), 824962 Car2TERA (sub-THz radar/telecom, graphene MMICs), 952792 2D-EPL (2D pilot line wafer prototyping), 101002772 SPINNER (graphene spintronics), 101006963 GreEnergy (graphene rectennas for energy harvesting), 101017186 AEOLUS (mid-IR photonic gas sensing, graphene photodetector). NON-EMBEDDING SWEEP over the 18 survivors' objective + report_text (summary/workPerformed/finalResults/teaser) on antibacterial|antimicrob|antibiotic|bacteri|pathogen|biofilm|infection: objective hits only PANG and PEST-BIN; report hits PANG, PEST-BIN and mCBEEs (adjudicated OUT above on the quoted context). DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10, same question): four projects satisfy the textual requirement but fail the country side of the filter - 966720 GRAPHFITI 'Graphene to Fight Antimicrobial Resistance' (rank 1 in all four conditions, graphene membranes for antibiotic susceptibility testing), 664782 VANGUARD (antibacterial graphene-oxide hydrogel coatings for implants, rank 3), 753636 NOVA (antimicrobial graphene-oxide-lanthanide composites for bone infection), 802093 ENIGMA (graphene drums detecting bacterial nanomotion for antibiotic resistance testing). All four carry the graphene euroSciVoc tag and have zero SE organisations, so the filter alone removes them; unscoped retrieval ranks GRAPHFITI above both gold members. TEXT SIDE: no stored column records what a project does with graphene, so the filter alone cannot answer. TERM-STYLE: exact-term - the question reuses 'graphene', 'antibiotic-resistant' and 'bacterial infections', all present verbatim in the gold texts; scoped lexical ranks PEST-BIN 1 and PANG 2, consistent with real term overlap. POOLING: scoped pooled search (k=10, scope=18 survivors) returned 10 candidates and ranked both gold members 1-2 in every condition; adjudication itself came from the exhaustive read of all 18, not from pooling.

text: Among Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that have an Italian participating organisation, what approaches to monitoring volcanic unrest and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Eight of the fifteen Italian-participating volcanology projects develop such approaches, in three families. New instrumentation: NEWTON-g builds a field gravity imager - an array of low-cost MEMS relative gravimeters anchored on an absolute quantum gravimeter - deployed at Etna to image subsurface mass change continuously, while SiC nano for PicoGeo develops 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters (target resolution 10-12) to reveal the slow strain transients that precede eruptions, seeding a 'Pico strain Etna Lab'. Automated interpretation of monitoring signals: VULCAN.ears builds a volcano-independent automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system, based on structured Hidden Markov Models and a Parallel System Architecture, so observatories can classify precursory seismicity in real time, and ARISE2 turns its infrasound and lidar network into a Volcano Information System, calibrated using Etna monitoring, that estimates ash plume height and mass eruption rate remotely for aviation security. Modelling, imaging and shared infrastructure: PICVOLC jointly inverts seismic, gravity and deformation data with 3D Finite Element modelling to image the source of volcanic unrest at Nevado del Ruiz; IMPROVE images magma storage zones by combining seismic, geodetic, gravity and geochemical data with machine learning, and produced prototypes of advanced gas and steam monitoring devices as well as field-tested uses of fibre-optic sensing for volcano monitoring; ChEESE prepares exascale flagship codes for ensemble volcanic ash dispersal forecasting with satellite data assimilation and physics-based probabilistic volcanic hazard assessment; and EUROVOLC connects volcano observatories and research institutions, integrating modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions.
notes: FILTER: projects carrying a euroSciVoc path under volcanology (natural sciences/earth and related environmental sciences/geology/volcanology) that have at least one participating organisation in Italy (organization.country='IT', any role). Executed this pass: 15 survivors, against 62 projects carrying the volcanology tag overall, so 47 topic members fail the country filter. SCOPE STATED IN THE QUESTION: the question says 'classified under volcanology' because the euroSciVoc classification is an authoring scope the runtime scoped path cannot rebuild - src/retrieval/scoped.py whitelists only project/organization structured columns (country, role, dates, funding, scheme, sme, activityType) and excludes subject matter, so the scope it actually builds here is organization.country='IT'. Inside that wider scope there are Italian-participating projects that satisfy the textual ask but carry no volcanology tag - 101004188 DeepCube ('UC4a: Automatic volcanic deformation detection and alerting', InSAR modelling of 'ground deformation patterns of volcanic unrest'; Italian participant TRE ALTAMIRA SRL), 723986 EUNADICS-AV (near-real-time monitoring and data assimilation for airborne hazards including volcano eruptions) and 891467 ALARM (detection and nowcasting/forecasting of volcanic ash and SO2). Stating the classification in the question puts them out of scope as asked rather than leaving them as silent misses. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, S=15 <= 20; every survivor's objective+teaser read, plus report summary/finalResults for the four borderline cases 653980, 674907, 858092, 101025887). IN: 653980 ARISE2 - final results report a Volcano Information System implemented on the ARISE infrasound platform, calibrated using Etna monitoring, for remote monitoring of non-instrumented volcanoes and prediction of ash plume height and mass eruption rate (marginal member: this is post-eruption plume characterisation rather than unrest monitoring or eruption forecasting); 731070 EUROVOLC - networks volcano observatories, integrated modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions; 749249 VULCAN.ears - automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system (structured HMMs + Parallel System Architecture) for real-time monitoring and eruption forecasting; 793811 PICVOLC - joint 3D numerical inversion of seismic, gravity and deformation data with FEM to image the source of volcanic unrest; 801221 NEWTON-g - MEMS/quantum gravimeter array as a field gravity imager for real-time monitoring of subsurface mass change at Etna; 823844 ChEESE - exascale codes for volcano monitoring, ensemble ash dispersal forecast with data assimilation, early-warning and physics-based hazard assessment; 858092 IMPROVE - subsurface imaging of magma systems plus fibre-optic sensing and gas/steam monitoring device prototypes, explicitly to enhance eruption forecasting; 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo - 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters for detecting pre-eruptive strain transients, with a monitoring-network start-up at Etna. OUT: 658591 CIAO - petrology/geochemistry of Iranian ophiolite peridotites, no observation or forecasting method for active volcanoes; 674907 EVER-EST - generic Virtual Research Environment for Earth Science data and workflow preservation; its volcano/supersite use case consumes and shares data, it develops no monitoring or forecasting approach; 714936 TRUE DEPTHS - X-ray-diffraction elastic thermobarometry on UHP rocks to constrain subduction depths; 765710 INSIGHTS - statistics for particle physics, volcanology only as a secondment domain; 845115 ICELEARNING - AI classification of insoluble particles in ice cores (volcanic tephra as a particle class), a palaeoclimate analysis routine; 101024337 PUSKURUM - tephrostratigraphy of past Central Anatolian eruptions for retrospective hazard assessment, no monitoring or forecasting method developed (third parties installing instruments on Erciyes is a reported societal effect, not project work); 101025887 ENDGAME - shock-tube/jet-flow experiments and 3D magma-ascent modelling of basaltic fragmentation, process understanding rather than monitoring or forecasting capability. FILTER LOAD-BEARING: unscoped pooled search for the same question returns volcanology-tagged projects with no Italian participant that satisfy the textual requirement - 798480 VOLCANOWAVES (ES; automatic volcano-seismic detection for eruption forecast modelling), 866085 DEEPVOLC (UK; deep learning on Sentinel-1 deformation to forecast volcanic activity), 789887 TREMOR (IS; pre-eruptive tremor as an eruption precursor), 101003173 MAST (UK/CZ/FR; strain tomography of volcano deformation to interpret unrest signals), 787399 SEISMAZE (FR; tremor analysis for new monitoring and forecasting approaches). Verified by SQL that each carries the volcanology tag and has no IT organisation. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records what monitoring or forecasting approach a project develops; the answer exists only in objective and report free text. RETRIEVABILITY: scoped pooled search (k=10 over the 15 survivors) ranks all eight gold members in at least one condition's top-10 (PICVOLC 1/1/1/1, VULCAN.ears 7/2/2/2, SiC nano 2/6/4/3, ARISE2 8/3/6/4, EUROVOLC 3/4/3/6, IMPROVE 5/5/5/5, NEWTON-g 10/7/9/9, ChEESE 9/-/10/8 as lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank). TERM_STYLE exact-term: the question reuses vocabulary present verbatim in gold texts - 'volcanic unrest' (PICVOLC, EUROVOLC), 'eruption forecasting' / 'forecasting volcanic eruptions' (VULCAN.ears, SiC nano), 'volcano monitoring' (ARISE2, ChEESE, IMPROVE); consistent with strong lexical ranks for four gold members. Adjudication came from the exhaustive read; the scoped pooled search supplied pooled_candidate_count (11 of the 15 survivors surfaced) and the rank matrix only.
